\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\ul\f0\fs24 ACTION 1: \par
\ulnone\par
Motion was made by Councilmember Saka, duly seconded and carried, to amend Council Bill 120777, by amending Section 1, adding a new Section K, as shown in the underlined language below: \par
\par
\ul K. Each of Seattle\rquote s eight designated historic districts are regulated by a citizens board and/or the Landmarks Preservation Board in accordance with processes and criteria detailed in Title 25 of the Seattle Municipal Code, which also sets forth the limited conditions under which a landmarked building may be demolished, and nothing in this ordinance supersedes those existing provisions and requirements.\par
\ulnone\par
\par
\ul ACTION 2: \par
\ulnone\par
Motion was made by Councilmember Morales, duly seconded and carried, to amend Council Bill 120777, by amending Section 1, adding a new Section D, and renumbering the subsequent sub-sections accordingly, as shown in the underlined language below: \par
\par
\ul D. These buildings represent a safety risk to the communities they are located in and the general public because they create opportunities for unauthorized trespass or occupancy, which may enable illegal or unsafe behavior and create additional fire risks. Unauthorized access to these buildings and the potential for drug use or other illegal behavior inside them may lead to further structural damage, decrease community safety, and endanger first responders.\par
\ulnone\par
\par
\ul ACTION 3: \par
\ulnone\par
Motion was made by Councilmember Kettle, duly seconded and carried, to amend Council Bill 120777, as shown in Attachment 1 to the Minutes.\par
\par
\par
\ul ACTION 4: \par
\ulnone\par
Motion was made by Councilmember Kettle, duly seconded and carried, to amend Council Bill 120777, by adding a new recital, as shown in the underlined language below: \par
\par
\ul WHEREAS, the intent of this ordinance is to permit the Seattle Fire Department to abate unsafe conditions on premises and/or property which includes construction sites, and to summarily abate conditions on such sites where there is an imminent danger to life and property; and\par
\ulnone\par
\par
\ul ACTION 5: \par
\ulnone\par
Motion was made by Councilmember Kettle, duly seconded and carried, to amend Council Bill 120777, as shown in Attachment 2 to the Minutes.\par
\ul\par
}

\par
\b 7.34.040 Enforcement and penalties\b0\par
The City Attorney may file a civil action in a court of competent jurisdiction for violations of this Chapter 7.34 for civil penalties of up to $7,500 per violation. \ul Each instance of coordinating services for each dwelling unit may be considered a separate violation.\ulnone  The court may award reasonable attorneys\rquote  fees and costs to the City Attorney if the City Attorney is the prevailing party.\par
\par
\b 7.34.050 Private right of action\b0\par
Any person injured by a violation of this Chapter 7.34 may bring a civil action in a court of competent jurisdiction against a landlord or other person violating this Chapter 7.34 to recover damages up to $7,500 per violation \ul in addition to any actual damages incurred\ulnone . The court may award reasonable attorneys\rquote  fees and costs to any person injured by a violation of this Chapter 7.34 if that person is the prevailing party.\par
\par

In favor: 6 - Hollingsworth, Kettle, Moore, Nelson, Rinck, Solomon\par
Opposed: 1 - Saka\par
Disqualified: 1 - Rivera\par

\ul ACTION 6:\ulnone\par
Motion was made by Councilmember Kettle and duly seconded to amend the recitals in Council Bill 121215 and add a new Section 9, as shown in the underlined and strike through language below:\par
\par
\ul The State of California has developed guidance for specific topics to guide analysis of impacts under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA).\par
The City of New York has developed a technical manual to guide analysis of proposals under the City Environmental Quality Review.\par
Unlike some states, like California, or cities, like New York City, neither Washington State nor the City of Seattle have developed detailed guidance on how SEPA analysis should be performed, resulting in each environmental impact statement using different approaches to analyze possible impacts.\par
Clear and uniform SEPA guidelines can increase clarity, trust, and consistency in environmental documents.\ulnone\par
\pard\sa160\sl276\slmult1\cf0\kerning2\f1 The Land Use Code requires \strike\f2 the development of\strike0\f1  director\rquote s reports for Type IV and V Council land use decisions but does not \ul clearly\ulnone  contemplate \ul reports for\ulnone  Council-sponsored land use decisions.\par
\pard\sa160\sl276\slmult1\qc * * *\par
\pard\cf1\kerning0\ul\f0 Section 9. The Office of Planning and Community Development (OPCD) should consult with other City agencies and City Boards and Commissions to develop a report on options for the creation of uniform guidelines for review under the City of Seattle\rquote s SEPA Policies, Seattle Municipal Code Section 25.05.675. OPCD should provide its report by March 1, 2027 and provide a briefing to the Land Use and Sustainability Committee or the City Council. The report should include:\par
1. An inventory of existing resources available to support analysis of specific elements of the environment, consistent with the City\rquote s environmental policies, including guidance provided by State agencies.\par
2. A recommendation on whether to prepare guidance for analysis of specific elements of the environment, or for a more comprehensive set of guidelines covering all elements of the environment.\par
3. If the report recommends development of uniform guidance on a subset of the elements of the environment, a prioritized list of elements.\par
4. A timeline and costs for implementing the recommendations of the report.\ulnone\par
\par
The motion carried by the following vote:\par
In favor: 9 - Foster, Hollingsworth, Juarez, Kettle, Lin, Rinck, Rivera, Saka, Strauss\par
Opposed: None\par
\par
}

\pard\sl276\slmult1\cf0 Of the money appropriated in the 2015 budget for the Seattle Department of Transportation\rquote s Mobility-Operations BCL and the Human Services Department\rquote s Community Support and Assistance BCL, $100,000 in each BCL may not be spent until the chair of the City Council Transportation Committee files with the City Clerk his certification that the Executive has submitted a report to the Transportation Committee on how the money is proposed to be spent for the Vehicle License Fee rebate and the Low Income Access programs or whether it will instead be used for other transportation priorities consistent with Seattle Transportation Benefit District Proposition 1.\par

c.\tab Strategies related to lowering the cost of processing and distributing Vehicle License Fee rebates; and\par
